source_caption:
The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift is the third movie in the Fast & Furious series, focusing on street racing culture in Tokyo, Japan. It follows Sean Boswell, an American teenager who gets into trouble for illegal racing and is sent to live with his father in Tokyo. There, he discovers the world of drift racing—a style of driving where cars slide through corners—and starts learning from a skilled racer named Han.

As Sean improves, he gets caught in conflicts with local racers, especially Takashi, known as the Drift King, who has ties to the Japanese underworld. The film blends high-speed action with themes of discipline and respect, showing Sean’s growth from a reckless outsider to a skilled driver. It’s especially known for introducing drifting to global audiences and for its unique Tokyo setting compared to earlier films.

source_details.synopsis: The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift is a 2006 American action film directed by Justin Lin and written by Chris Morgan. It is a standalone sequel to The Fast and the Furious (2001) and 2 Fast 2 Furious (2003), and the third installment in the Fast & Furious franchise. It is set between Fast & Furious 6 (2013) and Furious 7 (2015). It stars Lucas Black and Bow Wow. In the film, the car enthusiast Sean Boswell (Black) is sent to live in Tokyo with his estranged father and finds solace exploring the city's drifting community.
